items.explanation: 71-year-old woman with documented paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (Condition I48.0) followed in the cardiology clinic. Current outpatient orders as of 2026-09-24 are carvedilol, metoprolol tartrate and famotidine only - no oral anticoagulant has ever been ordered. CHA2DS2-VASc = 5 (hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, prior cerebral infarction with residual hemiplegia 2, female 1), so guideline-directed oral anticoagulation is recommended. Needs review for initiation of anticoagulation.

The anticoagulation clinic pharmacist note of 2026-09-10 documents a home INR of 3.4 and a warfarin decrease from 5 mg to 4 mg daily per protocol (a dose change permitted to clinic pharmacists under the standing order). The 2026-03-01 memo requires a confirmatory INR within 7 days, i.e. by 2026-09-17. The last INR in the chart is 2.6 on 2026-08-22, before the change; no INR has been resulted since the dose change and the due date has passed, so the requirement is overdue.

Citalopram 40 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug, was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-03-02 (it is absent from the 2025-12-15 medication list and first appears on 2026-03-02). The revised memo effective 2026-03-01 requires an ECG within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-03-16. ECG 104882441 was recorded on 2026-03-07 (sinus rhythm, QTc about 425 ms), within the window, so the requirement is complete.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug, was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2025-11-10 (absent from the 2025-08-02 medication list, first listed 2025-11-10). The memo in force at that time (2025-09-01) required an ECG within 30 days, i.e. by 2025-12-10; the revised 14-day memo only took effect 2026-03-01 and does not apply retrospectively. ECG 106885519 was recorded on 2025-11-24, 14 days after the start, so the requirement is complete (that ECG is the one showing QTc about 525 ms, logged separately as a QT safety item).

Escitalopram 10 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug, was first ordered at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-04-10. Because the start is after 2026-03-01 the revised memo applies and an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-04-24. The only ECG after the start is 107859369 on 2026-04-29, 19 days after the start - outside the required 14-day window (it would have satisfied the superseded 30-day memo). No qualifying ECG was obtained in time and the due date has passed, so the requirement is overdue; the 2026-04-29 tracing was normal (QTc about 390 ms).

Escitalopram 10 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug, was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-08-01 (not present on the 2026-06-24 medication list). Under the revised memo an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-08-15. The only ECG in the chart is 106035722 from 2025-12-25, long before the start, and no ECG has been obtained since; the due date has passed, so the requirement is overdue.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug, was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-08-10 (not on the 2026-02-27 medication list). Under the revised memo an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-08-24. The nurse telephone note of 2026-08-25 records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 2026-08-18 - inside the required window - but the report was requested by fax and has not been received, and no ECG for this patient exists in the chart. That outside tracing could have satisfied the requirement, so completion cannot be determined until the report is obtained.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily, a QT watch-list drug, was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-09-15 (not on the 2026-06-05 medication list). Under the revised memo an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-09-29. No ECG has been obtained since the start (the most recent tracing is 104253928 from 2025-03-09, QTc about 425 ms), but the due date is after the 2026-09-24 evaluation time, so the requirement is not yet due.

71-year-old man with documented atrial fibrillation (Condition 427.31), listed in every cardiology clinic note. The only current medication is tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily; no anticoagulant order is active and none appears in the chart. CHA2DS2-VASc = 3 (hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, coronary atherosclerosis/vascular disease 1), so anticoagulation is recommended. The only bleeding-related history is a coded 'hemorrhage complicating a procedure' with no narrative documentation, which does not by itself justify withholding therapy - needs prescriber review.

Apixaban 5 mg twice daily is a current order (2026-08-20 to 2026-12-28), yet the outside-records summary of 2026-08-12 documents an admission 2026-08-02 to 2026-08-05 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL, 2 units transfused) with apixaban explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. The anticoagulant is therefore active in the chart despite a documented major bleed and an explicit instruction that it should not continue without cardiology review. He is also on aspirin and clopidogrel, further increasing bleeding risk.

Two oral anticoagulants are simultaneously current: apixaban 5 mg twice daily (2026-07-15 to 2026-12-26) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (2026-07-15 to 2026-12-25). The clinic note of 2026-07-15 states the intent was to switch from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but the rivaroxaban order was never stopped and both remain active at the evaluation time, and both are listed as current medications in the note. Overlapping DOAC therapy is a major bleeding hazard and needs immediate reconciliation.

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both 12-lead ECGs recorded that same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular ventricular response with no discernible P waves at a ventricular rate of about 140/min, i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response - directly contradicting the documented rhythm and rate. The rhythm documentation needs correction and the rate control/anticoagulation plan needs review.

Patient is on amiodarone 200 mg daily, a clinic QT watch-list drug (current order 2026-08-22 to 2027-01-05). Her most recent ECG in the chart (101515306, 2022-04-27) shows sinus bradycardia at about 64/min with QT approximately 530 ms, giving a Bazett QTc of about 535 ms, which is at or above the clinic threshold of 500 ms and requires prescriber review. Most recent electrolytes are not contributory (potassium 4.1 mEq/L and magnesium 1.8 mg/dL, both 2026-02-14). A repeat ECG and review of the amiodarone are needed.

Patient takes amiodarone 200 mg daily, a clinic QT watch-list drug (current order 2026-07-29 to 2027-01-05). His most recent ECG (106885519, 2025-11-24) is sinus rhythm at 62/min with a QT of about 515-520 ms and a Bazett QTc of about 525 ms, at or above the clinic threshold of 500 ms, so prescriber review is required. Most recent potassium 4.4 mEq/L and magnesium 2.2 mg/dL (both 2026-04-20) are normal, so the prolongation is not explained by electrolytes.

Patient takes citalopram 40 mg daily, a clinic QT watch-list drug (current order 2026-05-29 to 2026-12-25) and a dose above the 20 mg/day maximum usually advised when QT prolongation is a concern. Her most recent ECG (104821039, 2023-11-10) is sinus rhythm at 70/min with a broad T wave, QT about 500 ms and Bazett QTc about 540 ms, at or above the clinic threshold of 500 ms, so prescriber review is required. Most recent potassium 4.5 mEq/L (2026-01-21) and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (2023-12-01) are normal.

At the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-09-01 the clinician documented INR 1.6 (subtherapeutic) and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily. Under the 2026-03-01 clinic memo an INR is required within 7 days of a warfarin dose change made by a clinic clinician or pharmacist, so it was due by 2026-09-08. INR(PT) 2.3 was resulted on 2026-09-05, within the required window, so the monitoring requirement is complete.

findings.explanation: Most recent ECG for this patient (2022-04-27). Sinus rhythm at about 64/min with two interpolated ventricular ectopic beats; median RR about 1.01 s. Measured QT (median beat, from QRS onset to the end of the T wave) is about 530 ms, giving a Bazett QTc of about 535 ms, above the clinic QT-monitoring threshold of 500 ms. Patient is on amiodarone.

Most recent ECG for this patient (2026-01-21). Irregularly irregular ventricular response (RR 0.72-1.11 s) with no reproducible P wave (pre-QRS segments uncorrelated between beats) and a wide QRS: atrial fibrillation with intraventricular conduction delay, mean ventricular rate about 65/min.

Most recent ECG for this patient (2026-03-15). Irregularly irregular RR intervals (0.50-0.86 s, coefficient of variation 0.18, 80% of successive differences >50 ms) with no P waves: atrial fibrillation, mean ventricular rate about 84/min.

Most recent ECG for this patient (2025-11-24). Regular sinus rhythm at 62/min (RR 0.97 s) with P waves present. QT measured on the median beat is about 515-520 ms with a broad, late-peaking T wave; Bazett QTc about 525 ms, above the clinic threshold of 500 ms. Patient is on amiodarone.

Most recent ECG for this patient (2023-11-10). Regular sinus rhythm at 70/min (RR 0.85 s). The T wave is markedly broad and low amplitude, ending about 500 ms after QRS onset; Bazett QTc about 540 ms, above the clinic threshold of 500 ms. Patient is on citalopram 40 mg daily.

Most recent ECG for this patient (2026-06-10 19:36). Irregularly irregular ventricular response (RR 0.35-0.65 s, coefficient of variation 0.16, 55% of successive RR differences >50 ms) with no reproducible P wave before QRS on lead II/V1 and a fibrillatory baseline: atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, mean ventricular rate about 136/min. The companion tracing earlier the same day (107914094) shows the same rhythm.

Most recent ECG for this patient (2024-11-15). Irregularly irregular RR intervals (0.40-1.15 s, coefficient of variation 0.28) with no discernible organised P wave activity: atrial fibrillation, mean ventricular rate about 70/min. Consistent with the documented history of atrial fibrillation.

Most recent ECG for this patient (2024-09-17). Irregularly irregular ventricular response (RR 0.39-0.73 s, coefficient of variation 0.20, 67% of successive RR differences >50 ms) with absent P waves: atrial fibrillation, mean ventricular rate about 109/min. Consistent with the documented atrial fibrillation diagnosis.

Most recent ECG for this patient (2025-09-13). Irregularly irregular narrow-complex tachycardia (RR 0.31-0.60 s, coefficient of variation 0.20) with no P waves: atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, mean ventricular rate about 147/min.

Most recent ECG for this patient (2024-09-06). Grossly irregular ventricular response (RR 0.54-1.32 s, coefficient of variation 0.30, every successive RR difference >50 ms) with no organised atrial activity: atrial fibrillation, mean ventricular rate about 67/min.

Most recent ECG for this patient (2024-10-31). Irregularly irregular RR intervals (0.48-0.90 s, coefficient of variation 0.21) with a flat, P-wave-free baseline before each QRS: atrial fibrillation, mean ventricular rate about 89/min.
